references.text: Prohibition against spreading false rumors, which expands on the ban against gossiping among the people.
He who goes about as a slanderer reveals secrets. Proverbs warns against the backbiter who discloses confidential information.
Warns against associating with those who reveal secrets and those with loose lips, linked to the prohibition against gossip.
Ezekiel condemns slanderers who shed blood, connecting gossip with violence and guilt for bloodshed.
Jeremiah describes how the people go about as gossips and deceive one another, a direct violation of this commandment.
Exhortation to rescue those being led away to death, linked to the prohibition against standing idly by when your neighbor's life is in danger.
Naboth was killed because of false witnesses, an example of violating the ban against standing by your neighbor's blood.
Reuben tried to save Joseph from being killed by his brothers, a positive example of not standing passively by a neighbor's blood.
James warns against slandering one another, a New Testament parallel to the prohibition against gossip.
Jesus teaches that people will have to give an account for every careless word they speak, linked to responsibility for speech.
